messages.subject: Re: error when trying to create a MSImageSet object
messages.subject_clean: error when trying to create a MSImageSet object
messages.body_plain:
The "readImzML" and "readMSIData" functions create MSImageSet objects as output.

You want to save the returned object to a variable, and do the normalization on that.

data <- readImzML("filename", folder="path/to/folder", ...)
data2 <- normalize(data, ...)

where "..." are your additional options.

You don't need to do "generateImage", which is for simulating data, or "MSImageSet", which is for creating an MSImageSet from data that you've loaded some other way (i.e., not using "readImzML" or "readMSIData").

Also, when you do "pixel = 13260" in the "normalize" method, you're only going to be normalizing the mass spectra from pixel #13260. For other preprocessing methods, this can be useful for looking at different parameter settings, but when you want to process the full dataset, you should do it without the "pixel" and "plot" arguments, so that the full dataset gets processed (and so you don't have to wait for them all to get plotted).

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: segfault error during spatial clustering
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mridula,

The data are not actually stored as a data cube according to their image dimensions. Rather, each mass spectrum is stored as a column in a matrix with dimensions (# of m/z features) x (# of pixels), with the image coordinates stored in a separate data structure. The image dimensions do not need to conform to combine datasets, the mass spectra only need to have the same m/z values.

The pixel data is stored sparsely. Missing pixels don't need to be stored. The size of combining two datasets should be exactly their individual sizes added together.

-Kylie

messages.body_plain: I would like to plot ROC for particular masses in my SSCG data.

messages.subject: Re: error when trying to create a MSImageSet object
messages.subject_clean: error when trying to create a MSImageSet object
messages.body_plain:
You could do:

library(lattice)
pData(data5)$PC1 <- data5[[1]]$scores[,"PC1"]
pData(data5)$PC2 <- data5[[1]]$scores[,"PC2"]
xyplot(PC1 ~ PC2, data=pData(data5), groups=sample)

-Kylie
